issues.label: Which law governs forum clause interpretation
issues.why: The court deemed dispositive whether Delaware or California law governs interpretation of the bylaw forum selection clause.

issues.label: Enforceability standard for forum selection clauses
issues.why: California requires the resisting party show enforcement is unreasonable or violates public policy, framing the analytical burden.

issues.label: Whether clause covers inspection demand
issues.why: The stay depends on whether a shareholder inspection request falls within claims 'governed by the internal affairs doctrine.'

issues.label: Internal affairs doctrine applicability to inspection
issues.why: Determining if shareholder record inspection implicates a Delaware corporation's internal affairs affects clause coverage.

issues.label: Public policy exception to enforcement
issues.why: Salamon argues enforcement would strip unwaivable California inspection rights, invoking the public policy bar.

issues.label: Unwaivability of sections 1600/1601 rights
issues.why: The statutes state inspection rights may not be limited by articles or bylaws, potentially voiding the clause.

issues.label: Distinction between absolute and reasonable-purpose rights
issues.why: Section 1600 grants an absolute right to shareholder lists, while 1601 requires a reasonable purpose—each may be treated differently.

issues.label: Comparison of California and Delaware inspection scope
issues.why: Whether Delaware Section 220 adequately protects Salamon's rights bears on the public policy analysis.

issues.label: Whether inspection right can be relinquished
issues.why: Even if Delaware provides remedy, forcing a different forum/statute may effectively waive statutorily protected California rights.

issues.label: Effect of Delaware dismissal for jurisdiction
issues.why: The Chancery Court dismissed Orchid's action for lack of personal jurisdiction, undermining the availability of the chosen forum.

issues.label: Propriety of stay pending Delaware action
issues.why: With the Delaware action dismissed, staying California proceedings for a nonexistent parallel case may be improper.

issues.label: Whether alternative forum is actually available
issues.why: Enforceability requires an available adequate forum; dismissal for jurisdiction suggests Salamon cannot be sued in Delaware.

issues.label: Standard of review for stay order
issues.why: The appellate court must determine deference owed to the trial court's interpretation and discretion.

issues.label: Judicial notice of Delaware proceedings
issues.why: The court must decide how noticed Delaware filings and the dismissal opinion affect the analysis.

issues.label: Salamon's stated purposes as proper purpose
issues.why: Valuing shares and investigating mismanagement must be assessed as proper purposes under applicable law.

issues.label: Scope of gambling-related document requests
issues.why: Requests 10-11 concerning gambling law violations may exceed proper-purpose limits or implicate the extortion allegation.

issues.label: Subsidiary records inspection rights
issues.why: Whether inspection extends to Orchid Labs, a separate subsidiary corporation, raises distinct entitlement questions.

issues.label: Salamon's counsel's concession about choice-of-law
issues.why: Counsel mistakenly claimed the bylaws contain a choice-of-law provision, affecting waiver and the record.

issues.label: Contractual vs statutory nature of forum clause
issues.why: Whether a unilateral bylaw binds a non-consenting shareholder affects enforceability of the forum selection provision.
